correctness.rationale: For every q,k,c>0, nilpotence reduces to A nilpotent and X^j has off-diagonal A^(j-1)B. The index of X is d or d+1, with exactly q^((k-r)c) index-d extensions when A has r longest blocks. Jordan centralizer sizes give the complete finite index polynomial. The near-maximal formula uses the unique-longest-block decomposition for 2s<k, a classical nilpotent cycle-index coefficient, and an explicit normalized q-binomial identity; pointwise probability convergence to a mass-one law gives total variation. All boundary cases (including X=0 and k=1) and seven small direct matrix-power enumerations were checked; finite experiments alone do not prove the formulas.

evidence: Fulman, arXiv:math/0009182, provides unipotent affine-group cycle-index calculations in the one-column parabolic setting, a meaningful c=1 precedent.
Fulman--Guralnick, arXiv:2111.09433, §3 recalls general Jordan centralizer counts and studies mutually annihilating pairs, not fixed-image blocks of arbitrary quotient codimension.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The affine-group case can supply parts of c=1 after transposition and a scalar shift. The claimed distribution retains arbitrary c (especially c>=2), with an independent Bernoulli(q^-c) limit and a complete nonregular population; c=1 precedent alone does not imply the multi-column formula without a new rank/column argument. A more general uninspected parabolic cycle-index theorem remains a risk, not dismissed by failed search.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Prior regular-locus counts condition on im(B) being inside im(A), while the new polynomial counts all B, usually nonregular. Because the condition A^(d-1)B=0 depends on multiplicity of the largest Jordan block rather than rank(A), the known regular-locus rank/index enumerator does not determine the unrestricted polynomial. Published general orbit formulas plus the new conditional fibre count imply the result, as proven, but the inspected papers do not provide that fibre count or the uniform limit as claimed.

originality.rationale: The full all-nilpotent restricted-range index enumerator and exact Bernoulli edge limit are not mathematical consequences of the published Green/ideal classifications or the previous regular-only locus count. The Jordan class-size and q-binomial input are classical, and the affine one-column special-case relationship is explicitly acknowledged. Inspected nearby primary sources and semantic search results did not exhibit the combined arbitrary-codimension result, with a recorded residual parabolic-literature risk.
residual_risks: A general parabolic or incidence-algebra unipotent cycle-index theorem not identified in the search could imply the all-c spectrum.
The 2017 regular-part paper was assessed from public abstract rather than its complete text.
One-column affine enumerators and standard nilpotent Jordan counts are prior results; those specialized ingredients must not be represented as independent discoveries.
Publication-index searches and semantic similarity do not prove exhaustive priority.

value.rationale: The full nilpotency index spectrum of a canonical nonregular transformation semigroup is a natural algebraic invariant, distinct from regularity/Green relations and from full matrix nilpotence. Exact all-dimensional counts, the high-index band and the Bernoulli codimension effect quantify nonregular maps and their atypically long nilpotent chains, providing useful invariant data beyond routine known orbit-class counts. No downstream theorem is required for the natural complete enumerator.
